hook.text: You train a language model and measure its loss. That loss function is cross-entropy—pure information theory.

buildup.text: Cross-entropy measures the average bits needed to encode text using the model's predictions instead of reality.

discovery.text: If the model matches reality perfectly, cross-entropy equals true entropy. Any mismatch adds extra bits.

twist.text: KL divergence is the gap: cross-entropy minus true entropy. It measures how many bits the model wastes.

climax.text: Every LLM training run minimizes cross-entropy. Shannon's 1948 paper is literally the loss function of modern AI.

punchline.text: AI training loss is Shannon's entropy. History rhymes.

quiz.question: What does cross-entropy measure in NLP?
options: How many bits the model needs to encode real text
